claim: Mia40 consists of two functional elements: an N-terminal cysteine-proline-cysteine motif conferring substrate oxidation, and a C-terminal hydrophobic pocket for substrate binding.
source: Mia40 consists of two functional elements: an N-terminal cysteine-proline-cysteine motif conferring substrate oxidation, and a C-terminal hydrophobic pocket for substrate binding.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of Mia40's structure and function.

claim: The substrate-binding domain of Mia40 is both necessary and sufficient to promote protein import.
source: Thereby we show that the substrate-binding domain of Mia40 is both necessary and sufficient to promote protein import, indicating that trapping by Mia40 drives protein translocation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: An oxidase-deficient Mia40 mutant is inviable.
source: An oxidase-deficient Mia40 mutant is inviable, but can be partially rescued by the addition of the chemical oxidant diamide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by growth assays in Figure 2.

claim: An oxidase-deficient Mia40 mutant can be partially rescued by the addition of the chemical oxidant diamide.
source: An oxidase-deficient Mia40 mutant is inviable, but can be partially rescued by the addition of the chemical oxidant diamide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in Figure 3.

claim: Mia40 predominantly serves as a trans-site receptor of mitochondria that binds incoming proteins via hydrophobic interactions.
source: Our results indicate that Mia40 predominantly serves as a trans-site receptor of mitochondria that binds incoming proteins via hydrophobic interactions thereby mediating protein translocation across the outer membrane by a 'holding trap' rather than a 'folding trap' mechanism.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Mia40 mediates protein translocation across the outer membrane by a 'holding trap' rather than a 'folding trap' mechanism.
source: Our results indicate that Mia40 predominantly serves as a trans-site receptor of mitochondria that binds incoming proteins via hydrophobic interactions thereby mediating protein translocation across the outer membrane by a 'holding trap' rather than a 'folding trap' mechanism.
evidence: This is the main mechanistic conclusion of the study, supported by data showing that the substrate-binding domain is sufficient for import.

claim: The bacterial periplasm, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the IMS of mitochondria contain dedicated oxidation machineries (disulfide relays) to introduce disulfide bonds into a broad range of substrate proteins.
source: In most cellular compartments, cysteine residues are predominantly present in the reduced state. In contrast, the bacterial periplasm, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the IMS of mitochondria contain dedicated oxidation machineries (disulfide relays) to introduce disulfide bonds into a broad range of substrate proteins (Riemer et al., 2009; Kadokura et al., 2003; Bulleid and Ellgaard, 2011; Stojanovski et al., 2012; Modjtahedi et al., 2016; Riemer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: In the case of the periplasm and the ER, disulfide bond formation presumably serves the function of stabilizing the structures of (secretory) proteins.
source: At least in the case of the periplasm and the ER, disulfide bond formation presumably serves the function of stabilizing the structures of (secretory) proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about protein folding in these compartments.

claim: Mitochondria consist of about 600 (yeast) to 1500 (humans) nuclear encoded proteins.
source: Mitochondria consist of about 600 (yeast) to 1500 (humans) nuclear encoded proteins (Pagliarini et al., 2008; Vögtle et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Proteins destined for the matrix of mitochondria contain presequences (or matrix-targeting signals) at their N termini.
source: Proteins destined for the matrix of mitochondria contain presequences (or matrix-targeting signals) at their N termini that target these proteins through the protein-conducting channels of the translocase of the outer membrane (TOM complex) and the inner membrane (TIM23 complex).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about mitochondrial protein targeting.

claim: After import into the mitochondria the presequences are proteolytically removed by the matrix processing peptidase MPP.
source: After import into the mitochondria the presequences are proteolytically removed by the matrix processing peptidase MPP (von Heijne, 1986; Vögtle et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Most IMS proteins do not contain N-terminal targeting signals but instead contain patterns of cysteine residues within their mature sequence that serve as targeting signals.
source: Most IMS proteins do not contain N-terminal targeting signals but instead contain patterns of cysteine residues within their mature sequence that serve as targeting signals (Koehler, 2004; Sideris and Tokatlidis, 2007; Sideris et al., 2009; Milenkovic et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In yeast, five 'twin Cx3C' (also called small Tim proteins) play a role as chaperones for carrier proteins in the IMS.
source: In yeast, five 'twin Cx3C' (also called small Tim proteins) play a role as chaperones for carrier proteins in the IMS (Curran et al., 2002b; 2002a; Koehler et al., 1998; Sirrenberg et al., 1998; Luciano et al., 2001; Vial et al., 2002)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: In yeast, 13 'twin Cx9C' proteins contribute to the stabilization and assembly of inner membrane proteins.
source: and 13 'twin Cx9C' proteins contribute to the stabilization and assembly of inner membrane proteins (Potting et al., 2010; Vögtle et al., 2012; Longen et al., 2009; Modjtahedi et al., 2016; Horn et al., 2010; Bode et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Erv1 is an FAD-binding sulfhydryl oxidase which can 'generate' disulfide bonds de novo.
source: Erv1 is an FAD-binding sulfhydryl oxidase which can 'generate' disulfide bonds de novo thereby transferring electrons either directly to molecular oxygen or to cytochrome c of the respiratory chain (Lee et al., 2000; Dabir et al., 2007; Ang and Lu, 2009; Tienson et al., 2009; Bien et al., 2010; Mesecke et al., 2005; Allen et al., 2005; Bihlmaier et al., 2007; Fass, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Erv1 transfers electrons either directly to molecular oxygen or to cytochrome c of the respiratory chain.
source: Erv1 is an FAD-binding sulfhydryl oxidase which can 'generate' disulfide bonds de novo thereby transferring electrons either directly to molecular oxygen or to cytochrome c of the respiratory chain (Lee et al., 2000; Dabir et al., 2007; Ang and Lu, 2009; Tienson et al., 2009; Bien et al., 2010; Mesecke et al., 2005; Allen et al., 2005; Bihlmaier et al., 2007; Fass, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The oxidoreductase Mia40 contains a redox-active cysteine-proline-cysteine (CPC) motif.
source: The oxidoreductase Mia40 contains a redox-active cysteine-proline-cysteine (CPC) motif (Terziyska et al., 2009; Chacinska et al., 2004; Banci et al., 2009; 2010; Kawano et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Erv1 maintains the CPC motif of Mia40 in an oxidized conformation which then permits the transfer of disulfide bonds to Mia40 substrates during their translocation into the IMS.
source: Erv1 maintains this motif in an oxidized conformation which then permits the transfer of disulfide bonds to Mia40 substrates during their translocation into the IMS (von der Malsburg et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Mia40 substrates are often small proteins that are unstructured in the reduced form but very stable as soon as they are oxidized.
source: Mia40 substrates are often small proteins that are unstructured in the reduced form but very stable as soon as they are oxidized (Morgan et al., 2009; Curran et al., 2004; 2002a; Baker et al., 2012; Banci et al., 2009; 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: According to the folding trap model, oxidation traps the incoming polypeptides in the IMS so that oxidation-induced folding drives their net translocation into the IMS.
source: It was proposed that oxidation traps the incoming polypeptides in the IMS so that oxidation-induced folding drives their net translocation into the IMS ('folding trap model') (Lutz et al., 2003; Koehler, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a previously proposed model, supported by citations.

claim: Structural analysis revealed the presence of a hydrophobic substrate-binding pocket on the surface of Mia40.
source: Structural analysis revealed the presence of a hydrophobic substrate-binding pocket on the surface of Mia40 (Figure 1A); like the CPC motif this substrate-binding region of Mia40 is essential for its function in the import and folding of IMS proteins and mutants were shown to be inviable (Banci et al., 2009, 2010; Kawano et al., 2009; Weckbecker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction, supported by citations, and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The substrate-binding region of Mia40 is essential for its function in the import and folding of IMS proteins and mutants were shown to be inviable.
source: like the CPC motif this substrate-binding region of Mia40 is essential for its function in the import and folding of IMS proteins and mutants were shown to be inviable (Banci et al., 2009, 2010; Kawano et al., 2009; Weckbecker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The substrate-binding region of Mia40 is essential for the binding and hence the oxidation of Mia40 substrates as well as for binding to Erv1.
source: This region is essential for the binding and hence the oxidation of Mia40 substrates as well as for binding to Erv1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Mia40 function.

claim: Mia40 substrates contain internal signals, known as MISS or ITS sequences, which specifically dock onto the substrate-binding region.
source: Mia40 substrates contain internal signals, known as MISS or ITS sequences, which specifically dock onto this binding region thereby selecting cysteine residues for interaction with the redox-active cysteine pair in Mia40 (Koch and Schmid, 2014b; Sideris and Tokatlidis, 2007; Sideris et al., 2009; Peleh et al., 2014; Milenkovic et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Mia40-SPS mutant contains a properly oxidized substrate-binding domain.
source: Whereas the Mia40-SPS mutant contained a properly oxidized substrate-binding domain (Figure 1E, middle panel: green arrow), the structural disulfides were not formed in the Mia40-FE mutant (Figure 1E, right panel: red arrow) indicating that the negative charges prevented the folding of the substrate-binding domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The structural disulfides were not formed in the Mia40-FE mutant.
source: Whereas the Mia40-SPS mutant contained a properly oxidized substrate-binding domain (Figure 1E, middle panel: green arrow), the structural disulfides were not formed in the Mia40-FE mutant (Figure 1E, right panel: red arrow) indicating that the negative charges prevented the folding of the substrate-binding domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The negative charges in the Mia40-FE mutant prevented the folding of the substrate-binding domain.
source: the structural disulfides were not formed in the Mia40-FE mutant (Figure 1E, right panel: red arrow) indicating that the negative charges prevented the folding of the substrate-binding domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In the Mia40-STOP variant, different redox states of the CPC motif were observed indicating that its cysteine residues are partially oxidized even in the complete absence of the substrate-binding domain.
source: In the Mia40-STOP variant, different redox states of the CPC motif were observed (Figure 1F) indicating that its cysteine residues are partially oxidized even in the complete absence of the substrate-binding domain (cf. Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Neither Mia40-SPS, nor Mia40-FE rescued the loss of the endogenous Mia40.
source: Although the different Mia40 variants were efficiently expressed in these strains and correctly targeted to the mitochondrial IMS (Figure 2D,E and data not shown), neither Mia40-SPS, nor Mia40-FE rescued the loss of the endogenous Mia40.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mia40 remained essential even upon simultaneous co-expression of Mia40-SPS and Mia40-FE or of Mia40-SPS and Mia40-STOP.
source: It should be noted that Mia40 remained essential even upon simultaneous co-expression of Mia40-SPS and Mia40-FE or of Mia40-SPS and Mia40-STOP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mia40 variants lacking either the redox-active cysteine pair or the substrate-binding pocket cannot cross-complement each other and both elements need to be present in close proximity in the same protein.
source: Hence, Mia40 variants lacking either the redox-active cysteine pair or the substrate-binding pocket cannot cross-complement each other and obviously both elements need to be present in close proximity in the same protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the complementation experiments.

claim: Diamide is a thiol-specific chemical oxidant that induces disulfide bond formation in proteins.
source: Diamide is a thiol-specific chemical oxidant that induces disulfide bond formation in proteins (Frand and Kaiser, 1998; Hansen et al., 2009) and which was shown to efficiently oxidize proteins of the mitochondrial IMS when added to the growth medium of yeast cells (Kojer et al., 2012; 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Diamide efficiently oxidizes proteins of the mitochondrial IMS when added to the growth medium of yeast cells.
source: Diamide is a thiol-specific chemical oxidant that induces disulfide bond formation in proteins (Frand and Kaiser, 1998; Hansen et al., 2009) and which was shown to efficiently oxidize proteins of the mitochondrial IMS when added to the growth medium of yeast cells (Kojer et al., 2012; 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Diamide is able to partially rescue the growth defect of the oxidation-deficient Mia40 mutant.
source: Interestingly, we observed a ring of growing colonies around the diamide-containing filter in cells expressing Mia40-SPS but not in cells expressing Mia40-FE. We conclude that diamide is able to partially rescue the growth defect of the oxidation-deficient Mia40 mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the presence of a chemical oxidizer, the hydrophobic binding pocket of Mia40 is apparently sufficient – and still essential - for viability.
source: Thus, in the presence of a chemical oxidizer, the hydrophobic binding pocket of Mia40 is apparently sufficient – and still essential - for viability.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the diamide rescue experiments.

claim: Mia40-SPS was able to efficiently promote the import of the cysteine-less protein 10CS whereas 10CS was not taken up by Mia40-FE mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, Mia40-SPS was able to efficiently promote the import of this protein whereas 10CS was not taken up by Mia40-FE mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Diamide did not affect the import of 10CS into either Mia40-SPS or Mia40-FE mitochondria.
source: However, diamide did not affect the import into either mutant suggesting that it has no effect on the functionality of Mia40-SPS or Mia40-FE.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Diamide does not induce non-canonical disulfides between Mia40-SPS and imported proteins but presumably acts on the imported substrates after their translocation into the mitochondria thereby stabilizing their structure.
source: Hence, diamide does not induce non-canonical disulfides between Mia40-SPS and imported proteins but presumably acts on the imported substrates after their translocation into the mitochondria thereby stabilizing their structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the diamide experiments.

claim: The redox-inactive Mia40-SPS mutant is still functional in the import of a cysteine-free model protein and sufficient for cell survival in the presence of the chemical oxidizer diamide.
source: In summary, we conclude that the redox-inactive Mia40-SPS mutant is still functional in the import of a cysteine-free model protein and sufficient for cell survival in the presence of the chemical oxidizer diamide.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary conclusion from the diamide experiments.

claim: Mia40-SPS efficiently drives the import reaction of both Tim9 and Atp23.
source: To this end, we imported radiolabeled Tim9 and Atp23, two proteins that are imported in a strictly Mia40-dependent reaction (Chacinska et al., 2004; Naoé et al., 2004; Weckbecker et al., 2012). Mia40-SPS was fully sufficient to drive the import reaction of both proteins (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mia40-driven oxidation is not critical for protein translocation into mitochondria.
source: We conclude that Mia40-driven oxidation is not critical for protein translocation into mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the import experiments with Mia40-SPS.

claim: The redox-active cysteines of Mia40 were dispensable for protein import, but the hydrophobic binding domain was essential since no import of Mia40 substrates was observed with the Mia40-STOP mutant.
source: Whereas the redox-active cysteines were dispensable for protein import, the hydrophobic binding domain was essential since no import of Mia40 substrates was observed with the Mia40-STOP mutant (Figure 4B, E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Overexpression of Erv1 in the Mia40-SPS background resulted in a considerable reduction of the import of Atp23 and Cmc1 into the IMS.
source: However, when we overexpressed Erv1 in the Mia40-SPS background, we did not observe a stimulation, but rather a considerable reduction of the import of Atp23 and Cmc1 into the IMS (Figure 4H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4H,I.

claim: The reduction of import upon Erv1 overexpression is most likely the consequence of a competitive binding of Erv1 and the incoming polypeptides to the substrate-binding pocket of Mia40.
source: This reduction is most likely the consequence of a competitive binding of Erv1 and the incoming polypeptides to the substrate-binding pocket of Mia40 (Banci et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the Erv1 overexpression data, supported by a citation.

claim: Considerable fractions of Tim9 and Cmc1 were co-isolated with Mia40-SPS during import reactions, albeit not covalently bound via disulfides.
source: When Mia40-SPS was isolated by immunoprecipitation during the import reactions, considerable fractions of Tim9 and Cmc1 were co-isolated (Figure 5A,B), albeit not covalently bound via disulfides (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The co-isolation of Tim9 and Cmc1 with Mia40-SPS indicates a tight association of the incoming proteins with the substrate-binding pocket of Mia40.
source: This indicates a tight association of the incoming proteins with the substrate-binding pocket of Mia40.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Mia40 substrates (Cox19, Tim9, Atp23) were not co-isolated with the Mia40-STOP variant.
source: In contrast, Mia40 substrates (Cox19, Tim9, Atp23) were not co-isolated with the Mia40-STOP variant (Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5 supplements.

claim: Tim9 and Cmc1 were not coisolated with Erv1, not even when Erv1 was overexpressed in the Mia40-SPS background.
source: Tim9 and Cmc1 were also not coisolated with Erv1, not even when Erv1 was overexpressed in the Mia40-SPS background (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), indicating that Erv1 does not interact with these proteins directly or the interaction is too transient or weak to be detected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5 supplement 3.

claim: The substrate-binding pocket of Mia40 is necessary and sufficient for protein import of Mia40 substrates whereas the redox activity of Mia40 is apparently dispensable.
source: In summary, we conclude that the substrate-binding pocket of Mia40 is necessary and sufficient for protein import of Mia40 substrates whereas the redox activity of Mia40 is apparently dispensable.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary conclusion from the import and co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Expression of Mia40-SPS in Mia40-depleted cells resulted in partial restoration of the levels of Mia40 substrates.
source: However, when Mia40-SPS was expressed in Mia40-depleted cells, we observed that the levels of Mia40 substrates were partially restored (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Both disulfides in Tim10 were properly formed in the Mia40-SPS mutant.
source: When we tested the redox states of the Mia40 substrate Tim10 in the Mia40-SPS mutant we found, that both disulfides in Tim10 were properly formed (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The redox-active CPC motif in Mia40 accelerates substrate oxidation, but it is not absolutely essential for protein oxidation in the IMS.
source: This suggests that the redox-active CPC motif in Mia40 accelerates substrate oxidation, but it is not absolutely essential for protein oxidation in the IMS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the Tim10 oxidation data.

claim: The presence of a functional substrate-binding pocket in Mia40 was critical for the accumulation of Mia40 substrates in vivo as Atp23 and Cmc1 were not detectable in Mia40-STOP mitochondria unless Mia40-SPS was co-expressed.
source: The presence of a functional substrate-binding pocket in Mia40 was critical for the accumulation of Mia40 substrates in vivo as Atp23 and Cmc1 were not detectable in Mia40-STOP mitochondria unless Mia40-SPS was co-expressed (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The ability of Mia40-SPS to partially restore the levels of Cox19, Atp23, and Cmc1 was also observed in cells of temperature-sensitive mia40 mutant that were grown under restrictive conditions.
source: The ability of Mia40-SPS to partially restore the levels of Cox19, Atp23, and Cmc1 was also observed in cells of temperature-sensitive mia40 mutant that were grown under restrictive conditions (Figure 6E), again indicating that the substrate-binding pocket is sufficient for protein import.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Overexpression of Erv1 did not further increase the levels of IMS proteins in the Mia40-SPS mutant but rather strongly diminished them.
source: Overexpression of Erv1 did not further increase the levels of IMS proteins in the Mia40-SPS mutant but rather strongly diminished them (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: In the wild type, Cox19-HA was rapidly oxidized and within less than 2 min the two disulfide bonds were formed.
source: In the wild type, Cox19-HA was rapidly oxidized and within less than 2 min the two disulfide bonds were formed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: In the temperature-sensitive mia40-4 mutant, the oxidation of Cox19-HA was considerably slower and only after 4 to 8 min, half of the protein was oxidized.
source: In the temperature-sensitive mia40-4 mutant, the oxidation of Cox19-HA was considerably slower and only after 4 to 8 min, half of the protein was oxidized.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: The oxidation of Cox19-HA was not accelerated by expression of Mia40-SPS.
source: The oxidation was not accelerated by expression of Mia40-SPS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: The primary function of Mia40 is a role as a trans-site receptor that drives the translocation of proteins across the outer membrane.
source: From the partial restoration of the IMS import by Mia40-SPS we conclude that the primary function of Mia40 is a role as a trans-site receptor that drives the translocation of proteins across the outer membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the in vivo accumulation experiments.

claim: Mia40 also facilitates protein oxidation, however, this function appears to be important only after the translocation reaction, presumably to fold IMS proteins into a functional and protease-resistant confirmation.
source: In addition, it also facilitates protein oxidation, however, this function appears to be important only after the translocation reaction, presumably to fold IMS proteins into a functional and protease-resistant confirmation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion about the role of oxidation.

claim: Overexpression of Mia40 leads to much higher cellular levels of Mia40 substrates, such as Atp23, Tim10 and Cmc1.
source: As shown in Figure 7A, overexpression of Mia40 leads indeed to much higher cellular levels of Mia40 substrates, such as Atp23, Tim10 and Cmc1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The endogenous levels of Mia40 are obviously rate-limiting under physiological conditions.
source: Thus, the endogenous levels of Mia40 are obviously rate-limiting under physiological conditions, suggesting that only a fraction of the Mia40 substrates that are initially synthesized in the cytosol finally accumulate as stable proteins in vivo and that overexpression of Mia40 increases this fraction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the Mia40 overexpression data.

claim: Only a fraction of the Mia40 substrates that are initially synthesized in the cytosol finally accumulate as stable proteins in vivo and overexpression of Mia40 increases this fraction.
source: Thus, the endogenous levels of Mia40 are obviously rate-limiting under physiological conditions, suggesting that only a fraction of the Mia40 substrates that are initially synthesized in the cytosol finally accumulate as stable proteins in vivo and that overexpression of Mia40 increases this fraction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the Mia40 overexpression data.

claim: Increased amounts of cytochrome b2 were observed upon overexpression of Mia40.
source: We even observed increased amounts of cytochrome b2, a protein that is imported into the IMS on a stop-transfer pathway (Glick et al., 1992; Gärtner et al., 1995; Esaki et al., 1999) and that was not expected to be influenced by the presence of Mia40.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The upregulation of Mia40 considerably improved the import of Cmc1, Atp23 and Tim9.
source: We found consistently, that the upregulation of Mia40 considerably improved the import of Cmc1, Atp23 and Tim9.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Upregulation of Mia40 did not increase, but rather reduced, the import of cytochrome b2.
source: In contrast, upregulation of Mia40 did not increase, but rather reduced, the import of cytochrome b2 (Figure 7D), a well-characterized substrate of the presequence pathway (Hartl et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Depletion of Mia40 impaired the processing of cytochrome b2.
source: Depletion of Mia40 did hardly affect the import of cytochrome b2, however, it impaired its processing.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The impaired processing of cytochrome b2 upon Mia40 depletion is presumably explained by the fact that the Mia40 substrate Som1 is a component of the inner membrane protease complex that mediates the maturation of cytochrome b2.
source: This is presumably explained by the fact that the Mia40 substrate Som1 is a component of the inner membrane protease complex that mediates the maturation of cytochrome b2 (Jan et al., 2000; Nunnari et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the cytochrome b2 processing data, supported by citations.

claim: The strong rate-limiting function of Mia40 on the import of its substrates is obviously highly relevant to the protein composition of the IMS in general and critical even for proteins which are imported in a Mia40-independent fashion.
source: Thus, the strong rate-limiting function of Mia40 on the import of its substrates is obviously highly relevant to the protein composition of the IMS in general and critical even for proteins which are imported in a Mia40-independent fashion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the Mia40 overexpression experiments.

claim: Both the redox-active cysteine pair and the substrate-binding region of Mia40 are essential and mutants lacking individual elements cannot cross-complement each other.
source: Here we show that both the redox-active cysteine pair and the substrate-binding region of Mia40 are essential and mutants lacking individual elements cannot cross-complement each other.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the main findings.

claim: Cysteines in the CPC motif of Mia40 are dispensable for the import reaction of all Mia40 substrates tested.
source: However, we found that cysteines in the CPC motif of Mia40 are dispensable for the import reaction of all Mia40 substrates we tested.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the main findings.

claim: The reversible nature of the outer membrane translocation of Mia40 substrates is experimentally well documented.
source: The reversible nature of the outer membrane translocation of Mia40 substrates is experimentally well documented (Lutz et al., 2003; Bragoszewski et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The affinity to the substrate-binding pocket provides the driving force for the translocation reaction rather than protein oxidation.
source: However, our observation that the Mia40-SPS variant can efficiently drive the import reaction suggests that the affinity to the substrate-binding pocket provides the driving force for the translocation reaction rather than protein oxidation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Mia40 serves as a 'trans-site receptor' on the IMS site of the TOM complex that mediates protein translocation across the outer membrane.
source: Hence, we propose that Mia40 serves as a 'trans-site receptor' on the IMS site of the TOM complex that mediates protein translocation across the outer membrane (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as the main model proposed by the study.

claim: The oxidoreductase activity of Mia40 is important, but it apparently plays a role after translocation.
source: The oxidoreductase activity of Mia40 is obviously important, but it apparently plays a role after translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Mutants of small Tim proteins, in which all cysteine residues were replaced by serine residues, accumulated to wild type levels in the IMS as soon as the iAAA protease Yme1 was deleted.
source: This is consistent with a recent study which showed that mutants of small Tim proteins, in which all cysteine residues were replaced by serine residues, accumulated to wild type levels in the IMS as soon as the iAAA protease Yme1 was deleted (Baker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The presence of diamide can partially suppress the growth defect of Mia40-SPS cells suggesting that the substrate-specificity of the mitochondrial disulfide relay is not absolutely necessary.
source: Surprisingly, the presence of diamide can partially suppress the growth defect of Mia40-SPS cells suggesting that the substrate-specificity of the mitochondrial disulfide relay is not absolutely necessary.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the diamide rescue experiments.

claim: Even in the presence of diamide, Mia40-SPS cells were very sick and protein oxidation in the IMS is obviously still an essential process.
source: However, it should be noted that, even in the presence of diamide, Mia40-SPS cells were very sick and protein oxidation in the IMS is obviously still an essential process.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a qualification of the diamide rescue findings.

claim: Mia40 is rate-limiting for the import into mitochondria as overexpression of Mia40 leads to a considerable increase of the levels of many Mia40 substrates.
source: Our observations indicate that Mia40 is rate-limiting for the import into mitochondria as overexpression of Mia40 leads to a considerable increase of the levels of many Mia40 substrates.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the overexpression experiments.

claim: A fraction of the Mia40 substrates that are initially synthesized in the cytosol are degraded in the cytosol or the IMS.
source: Apparently, a fraction of the Mia40 substrates that are initially synthesized in the cytosol are degraded in the cytosol or the IMS, an assumption that is supported by pulse labeling experiments in whole cells (Wrobel et al., 2015; Longen et al., 2014; Kojer et al., 2015; Fischer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Increased levels of Mia40 might reduce the degradation either by accelerating the import or the folding reaction.
source: Increased levels of Mia40 might reduce the degradation either by accelerating the import or the folding reaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about the mechanism of Mia40 overexpression effects.

claim: Up- or down-regulation of the levels of Erv1 had no positive effect on the steady state levels of IMS proteins.
source: In contrast, up- or down-regulation of the levels of Erv1 had no positive effect on the steady state levels of IMS proteins again supporting the idea that the trapping rather than the oxidase function of Mia40 is decisive (Bien et al., 2010; Mesecke et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The strong increase in Mia40 substrates in Mia40-overexpressing cells suggests that more Mia40 leads to more import sites for Mia40 substrates.
source: The strong increase in Mia40 substrates in Mia40-overexpressing cells suggests that more Mia40 leads to more import sites for Mia40 substrates.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the overexpression data.

claim: It is conceivable that mitochondria contain specific import sites for different types of preproteins which differ at the level of the 'trans-site receptors' in the IMS.
source: It is conceivable that mitochondria contain specific import sites for different types of preproteins which differ at the level of the 'trans-site receptors' in the IMS (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about mitochondrial import organization.

claim: Matrix-targeted proteins might specifically encounter TOM complexes that are associated to Tim50 whereas IMS proteins might use TOM complexes that are in proximity to Mia40.
source: Thus, matrix-targeted proteins might specifically encounter TOM complexes that are associated to Tim50 (Lytovchenko et al., 2013; Marom et al., 2011) whereas IMS proteins might use TOM complexes that are in proximity to Mia40.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about import pathway organization, supported by citations.

claim: The Mic60 subunit of the MICOS complex presumably tethers Mia40 to a subpopulation of the TOM complex.
source: This hypothesis is supported by studies on the Mic60 subunit of the MICOS complex which presumably tethers Mia40 to a subpopulation of the TOM complex (von der Malsburg et al., 2011; Herrmann, 2011; Varabyova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The existence of a discrete translocation route into the IMS was recently proposed for Mia40 substrates on the basis of in organello competition import experiments.
source: The existence of a discrete translocation route into the IMS was recently proposed for Mia40 substrates on the basis of in organello competition import experiments (Gornicka et al., 2014) and, even much earlier, for the most abundant IMS protein, cytochrome c (Wiedemann et al., 2003; Diekert et al., 2001; Mayer et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The bacterial periplasm, the ER and the mitochondrial IMS are the three compartments in which dedicated machineries mediate the oxidative folding of a broad range of proteins.
source: The bacterial periplasm, the ER and the mitochondrial IMS are the three compartments in which dedicated machineries mediate the oxidative folding of a broad range of proteins (Riemer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Members of the thioredoxin protein family mediate protein oxidation in the periplasm (DsbA) and the ER (PDI).
source: Members of the thioredoxin protein family mediate protein oxidation in the periplasm (DsbA) and the ER (PDI).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as established knowledge.

claim: The thioredoxin-based oxidation system of the periplasm of the endosymbiont that served as the ancestor of mitochondria was replaced during evolution by the Mia40 system.
source: Apparently, the thioredoxin-based oxidation system of the periplasm of the endosymbiont that served as the ancestor of mitochondria was replaced during evolution by the Mia40 system.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an evolutionary interpretation.

claim: In its oxidizing power, Mia40 is weaker than DsbA, and in forming correct disulfides, it is slower than PDI.
source: This replacement during evolution was hardly driven to increase protein oxidation in the IMS since Mia40 is a poor catalyst: in its oxidizing power, it is weaker than DsbA, and in forming correct disulfides, it is slower than PDI (Koch and Schmid, 2014b; 2014a; Hudson and Thorpe, 2015; Tienson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Mia40 binds much stronger and for much longer interaction times to its substrates than DsbA or PDIs.
source: However, Mia40 binds much stronger and for much longer interaction times to its substrates than DsbA or PDIs (Koch and Schmid, 2014b; Mesecke et al., 2005; Naoé et al., 2004; Chacinska et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The ability of Mia40 to trap incoming preproteins efficiently at the trans-site of the TOM complex made Mia40 the superior oxidoreductase to mediate the translocation and oxidation of IMS proteins.
source: It therefore appears likely that the ability of Mia40 to trap incoming preproteins efficiently at the trans-site of the TOM complex made Mia40 the superior oxidoreductase to mediate the translocation and oxidation of IMS proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion about the evolutionary advantage of Mia40.
